newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand finished a largely uneventful Friday with a small spring in its step as it watched the demise of the U.S. dollar.
"The dollar's collapsing and the rand's getting something out of it but it isn't jumping for joy. The market really lost interest from about 0900 GMT," said one dealer.
The local unit was last priced at 4.6870/6900 to the dollar from 4.6850/6880 late Thursday and well off its worst level of 4.6970 but on wafer-thin turnover.
The dollar/mark dropped over a pfennig in morning U.S. dealings on fears of a switch by the German central bank to a variable repo next week.
Dealers were sure of a stronger open for the rand Monday and some touted a strategy of keeping shorter dollars.

"Should dollar/mark remain here we'll be lower. I wouldn't want to be long in this market, not with a sloppy dollar anyway. Cable's looking strong and crosses are looking weak and on the back of that the Reserve Bank may push it if he's forced to. I would rather be short than long," said one.
The rand ended the week wilted in cross rate dealings, last priced at last at 0.3882/3886 on the German mark from 0.3930/3936 late Thurssday.
Rand/yen was at 25.9419/9792 from 25.0288/0662 and against sterling, the rand was last trading at 7.5441/5513 from 7.4275/4346.
